subject: How an optical fibre guides light
audience: Readers of a technical project report without specialist optics training
takeaway: A core with a higher refractive index than its cladding can guide light by total internal reflection; the external coating has a protective role.

requiredText: θ is measured from the normal.
Total internal reflection occurs at the core–cladding boundary.
The coating protects the glass; index contrast guides the light.
sameAcrossVariants.scope: Straight ideal step-index fibre, ray model. Geometry and index contrast are illustrative; no dimensions, numerical aperture, dispersion or performance claims. The condition θ > θc applies to incidence at the internal boundary, not directly to the launch angle.

directions.editorial: A large engraved cross-section, a linked longitudinal detail, warm paper and open typography. The physical structure provides the visual anchor.
directions.technical: Orthographic end and side views on a restrained blueprint grid, precise ray geometry and a normal at the point of reflection.
directions.hybrid: A generated text-free glass cutaway as the hero, anchored editable annotations and a separate vector inset that carries the ray geometry.

review: Can the reader identify the three regions?
Does every leader end on its intended material?
Does the ray remain inside the core and reflect at its boundary?
Is θ clearly measured relative to the normal?
Do the same claims survive at 180 mm print width?
Can a label be changed without regenerating the artwork?

sources.title: OpenStax University Physics, Volume 3: Total Internal Reflection
